title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions on the Reasonable Allocation and Scientific Operation of Enforcement Powers
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Several Opinions on the Reasonable Allocation and Scientific Operation of Enforcement Powers"

Fa Fa [2011] No. 15

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The "Several Opinions on the Reasonable Allocation and Scientific Operation of Enforcement Powers" of the Supreme People's Court are hereby issued to you. Please carefully implement them in light of the actual work circumstances.

October 19, 2011

Several Opinions on the Reasonable Allocation and Scientific Operation of Enforcement Powers

In order to promote the fair, efficient, standardized, and clean operation of enforcement powers, achieve coordination and cooperation between case-filing, trial, enforcement and other institutions, and improve the unified management of enforcement work, the following opinions are put forward in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the provisions of relevant judicial interpretations.

I. Regarding the Separation of Enforcement Powers and Efficient Operation Mechanism

1. Enforcement powers are the powers of the people's court to lawfully adopt various enforcement measures and to review matters such as enforcement objections, reconsideration, and complaints, including enforcement implementation powers and enforcement review powers.

2. The enforcement bureau of a local people's court shall, in accordance with the separation of powers mechanism, establish enforcement implementation and enforcement review departments parallel to other trial divisions, which shall respectively exercise enforcement implementation powers and enforcement review powers.

3. The scope of enforcement implementation powers is mainly matters such as property investigation, control, disposition, delivery, and distribution, as well as measures such as fines and detention. Enforcement implementation powers shall be exercised by enforcement officers or judges.

4. The scope of enforcement review powers is mainly to review and handle matters such as enforcement objections, reconsideration, and complaints, as well as to decide on the transfer of enforcement jurisdiction. Enforcement review powers shall be exercised by judges.

5. The handling of enforcement implementation matters shall adopt an approval system; the handling of enforcement review matters shall adopt a collegiate panel system.

6. The people's court may divide the enforcement implementation process into different stages such as property investigation and control, property disposition, and distribution of money and goods, and specify time limits. These stages shall be handled centrally by different enforcement personnel, who shall supervise each other, achieve a separation of powers and checks and balances, and improve the quality and efficiency of enforcement work. The comprehensive management department of the enforcement bureau shall exercise node control and process management over the segmented enforcement.

7. If emergency circumstances during enforcement require the immediate adoption of enforcement measures, enforcement personnel may, upon instruction from the enforcement command center, lawfully adopt property preservation and other control measures such as sealing up, distraining, and freezing, and shall subsequently complete the approval formalities within two working days.

8. The people's court shall establish an enforcement petition review and handling mechanism within the enforcement bureau to effectively address issues of passive enforcement and non-standard enforcement. The enforcement petition review department may participate in receiving petitioners in enforcement-related petition cases, and shall adopt measures such as ranking and reporting, and supervising and urging the handling of cases to promote the timely resolution of enforcement-related petition cases.

9. Continue to promote the construction of a national court enforcement case information management system, and actively participate in the construction of a social credit system. The enforcement information department shall leverage its functional advantages, adopt various measures to expand the scope of inquiries, realize the sharing of all information on enforcement cases within the court system, promote the sharing of enforcement case information with credit information of other departments, and urge debtors to voluntarily perform obligations through credit punishment measures.

II. Regarding the Division of Labor and Collaboration between the Enforcement Bureau and Case-filing, Trial, and Other Institutions

10. Enforcement powers shall be exercised by the enforcement bureau of the people's court; a people's tribunal may, upon authorization of the enforcement bureau, enforce cases it has tried, but shall accept the management and professional guidance of the enforcement bureau.

11. When handling enforcement implementation, enforcement objections, enforcement reconsideration, enforcement supervision, enforcement coordination, enforcement requests for instructions, and other enforcement cases, as well as litigation cases related to enforcement such as third-party enforcement objection lawsuits, applying creditor enforcement objection lawsuits, enforcement distribution plan objection lawsuits, and subrogation property partition lawsuits, the case-filing institution shall conduct case-filing review and include them in the unified management system for trial and enforcement cases.

If a people's tribunal is authorized to enforce cases it has tried, it may handle the case-filing registration procedures on its own and include them in the unified management of enforcement cases.

12. Litigation cases related to enforcement, such as third-party enforcement objection lawsuits, applying creditor enforcement objection lawsuits, enforcement distribution plan objection lawsuits, and subrogation property partition lawsuits, shall be tried by the trial institution of the people's court in accordance with civil procedure. Gradually promote the specialization of trial of enforcement-related litigation; a people's court with appropriate conditions may establish a specialized trial institution to centrally hear enforcement-related litigation cases.

If a third party or party believes that the judgment or ruling based on which enforcement is sought is erroneous, it shall be tried by the original trial people court that rendered the effective judgment or ruling, or its superior people's court, in accordance with the trial supervision procedure.

13. For enforcement applications in administrative non-litigation cases and administrative litigation cases, the case-filing institution shall register them and then transfer them to the administrative trial institution for legality review; if a ruling is made to approve compulsory enforcement, the case-filing institution shall then complete the enforcement case-filing registration and transfer the case to the enforcement bureau for enforcement.

14. The implementation of compulsory liquidation shall be the responsibility of the enforcement bureau; substantive disputes in compulsory liquidation shall be tried by the civil trial institution.

15. Applications for property preservation before litigation or before enforcement application shall be reviewed and ruled upon by the case-filing institution; if a ruling is made for preservation, the case shall be transferred to the enforcement bureau for enforcement.

16. Applications for property preservation during litigation or advance execution shall be reviewed and ruled upon by the relevant trial institution; if a ruling is made for property preservation or advance execution, the case shall be transferred to the enforcement bureau for enforcement.

17. If a party or third party applies for reconsideration of a ruling on property preservation or advance execution, the case-filing institution or trial institution that made the ruling shall review it in accordance with Article 99 of the Civil Procedure Law.

If a party, third party, or interested party raises an objection to the implementation actions of property preservation or advance execution, the enforcement bureau shall conduct a review based on the nature of the objection in accordance with Article 202 or Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law.

If a party's or third party's objection is directed at both the ruling on property preservation or advance execution and the implementation actions, the case-filing institution or trial institution that made the ruling shall conduct a consolidated review in accordance with Articles 99 and 202 or 204 of the Civil Procedure Law, respectively.

18. The enforcement of property-related criminal penalties and non-criminal penalty measures with enforcement content shall be the responsibility of the enforcement bureau.

19. Applications for enforcement of effective legal documents rendered by foreign courts or arbitration institutions shall be reviewed by the trial institution; if a ruling is made to approve enforcement or an enforcement order is issued, the case shall be transferred to the enforcement bureau for enforcement.

20. If disputes arise between different courts over the subject matter of enforcement due to enforcement procedures, or between enforcement, bankruptcy, compulsory liquidation, trial, and other procedures, and they cannot reach an agreement through self-coordination, the matter shall be handled by the coordination and guidance department of the enforcement bureau of the common superior court of the disputing courts.

21. If it is necessary to change or add an enforcement subject during the enforcement process in accordance with the law, the enforcement bureau shall handle it in accordance with statutory procedures; if changes or additions require a separate lawsuit or the initiation of retrial, the trial institution shall handle it in accordance with statutory procedures.

22. The judicial auxiliary department shall be responsible for entrusting evaluations, auctions, and sales; objections raised against evaluations, auctions, and sales shall be reviewed by the enforcement bureau.

23. If an enforcement respondent raises a defense against enforcement of a domestic arbitration award, the enforcement bureau shall review it.

24. When handling civil, commercial, and incidental civil litigation cases, the case-filing and trial institutions shall, based on the actual circumstances of the case, provide necessary explanations and notifications to the parties regarding matters such as adding litigation parties, applying for property preservation before litigation, during litigation, and before enforcement application.

25. When handling civil, commercial, and incidental civil litigation cases, the case-filing and trial institutions shall, except in cases of default judgment where the identity and address of the parties cannot be accurately ascertained, include the party's ID number in the relevant legal documents and the service address in the case file.

26. When trying a case to confirm ownership (right confirmation litigation), the trial institution shall inquire into the property ownership status to be confirmed. If it finds that the property has already been sealed up, distrained, or frozen by the enforcement bureau, it shall suspend the trial; if the property for which a party requests confirmation of ownership has been disposed of by the enforcement bureau, the court shall dismiss the ownership confirmation case; if ownership is confirmed after the enforcement bureau has sealed up, distrained, or frozen the property, the ownership confirmation judgment or mediation agreement shall be revoked.

27. For legal documents that meet the statutory conditions for transferred enforcement, the trial institution shall promptly transfer them to the enforcement bureau for enforcement after the legal documents become effective.

III. Regarding the Unified Management of Enforcement Work

28. A people's court at or above the intermediate level shall exercise unified management over the enforcement work of the people's courts within its jurisdiction. If a lower people's court refuses to comply with the unified management of a higher people's court, the responsibility of the relevant responsible persons of the lower people's court shall be investigated in accordance with relevant provisions.

29. A higher people's court may organize centralized enforcement and special enforcement activities based on the enforcement work situation within its jurisdiction.

30. If the enforcement ruling or enforcement conduct of a lower people's court is illegal or erroneous, the higher people's court has the authority to instruct the lower people's court to correct it on its own or to correct it by means of a ruling or decision.

31. When organizing centralized enforcement, special enforcement, or other major enforcement activities, a higher people's court may uniformly command and deploy the enforcement personnel, judicial police, and enforcement equipment of lower people's courts.

32. Based on enforcement work needs, a higher people's court may consult with relevant government departments to develop enforcement equipment standards and business expense plans for the people's courts within its jurisdiction.

33. A higher people's court has the authority to appraise the enforcement work of lower people's courts and shall report the appraisal results to the lower people's courts.
